h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A direct conv3x3 on 0->3 already supplies spatial capacity at the output node, so an additional conv on 2->3 yields diminishing returns.
With 0->3 already convolved, a conv on 1->3 adds a partly redundant parallel conv route into the output, shrinking its marginal gain.
An identity bypass on 0->3 eases optimisation of the deepened 0->1->2->3 conv chain, matching the residual-plus-deep-conv pattern of top NAS-Bench-201 cells.
A parallel conv route on 1->3 already supplies output capacity, so degrading 2->3 to pooling costs less.
If 0->2 already convolves, a conv on 1->2 is a partly redundant second learnable input to node 2, reducing its marginal benefit.
With 1->2 absent, 0->2 is node 2's only input, so making it a conv determines everything flowing through 2->3 and matters more.
A skip on 1->3 forwards node 1's features to the output, which is only valuable when node 1 holds learned conv features.
An identity bypass on 0->3 around a conv route ending at 2->3 forms a residual block, raising the skip's value relative to when 2->3 is weak.
Identity on 0->3 plus a conv branch through 1->3 forms a classic residual block, so the skip helps more when 1->3 convolves.
Removing node 2's direct input is more harmful when 2->3 holds a conv, because the conv's capacity is wasted on a weakened or empty node 2.
